A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ResearchDB study despite changes to the title and layout. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of 104,482 papers, including topic, compute, dataset, and institutional trends, plus human-rated retrieval-generation results and an appendix case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original analyses and adds SurveyX comparison results, component ablations, and measurements of processing throughput and query latency.

M1.justification: The parsing, clustering, metadata filtering, and weighted semantic retrieval pipeline is retained. Query-dependent LLM weighting, emphasized in v2 Section 3.2, was already specified in v1 Appendix B. Expanded weighting explanations and newly specified matching rules do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 104,482-paper corpus covering 22 venues during 2020–2025 and retain the topic-based evaluation and speech-to-gesture case study. The added comparisons, ablations, and efficiency measurements do not introduce a new dataset or task domain.

E2.justification: The reported comparison set broadens substantially beyond direct ChatGPT-5 generation. v2 Figure 9 adds SurveyX, previously only discussed as related work, while Table 3 adds comparisons against retrieval without metadata filtering, without dynamic weighting, and using abstracts alone.

E3.justification: The existing Top-20-topic, five-rater, five-dimension Likert evaluation and appendix top-10 retrieval scoring protocol are retained. New experiments introduce controlled component removals, uniform weighting, abstract-only retrieval, and throughput/latency measurements. These are added evaluation conditions rather than revisions to the original rating protocol.

E4.justification: New Section 5.1 and Table 3 directly test the contributions of metadata filtering, dynamic weighting, and multiple semantic fields; v1 had no corresponding component ablations. Appendix D also adds an efficiency analysis. The existing qualitative case study remains substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the UMAP random seed of 42 and the statement that inter-rater agreement was measured using Cohen’s kappa, without reporting its value. The new ablation and efficiency results introduce no repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds SurveyX scores and ablation results, including accuracy of 4.50 for ResearchDB versus 4.12 without filtering, 3.86 without dynamic weighting, and 3.70 for abstract-only retrieval. Appendix D newly reports approximately 870 papers/hour, 120 processing hours, 960 GPU-hours, and 1.2-second average query latency. ResearchDB’s plotted readability changes from approximately 4.3 to 4.0 and usefulness from 4.1 to 4.4 between v1 Figure 10 and v2 Figure 9, without an explanation of these revisions. The scientometric results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same filtering, weighted relevance, Top-K retrieval, growth-rate, publication-year, and impact definitions. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs; the expanded adaptive-weighting discussion is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: a large literature corpus, an integrated profiling/retrieval framework, and empirical analyses of research trends. The shortened conclusion preserves this scope; the additional evaluations support existing claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of why filtering, weighting, and multiple fields help retrieval, while removing v1’s explicit discussion of coverage/readability tradeoffs. It also drops explicit cautions about incomplete public metadata and overgeneralization, and adds future work on parsing and venue coverage. Its new claim of leading on every ablation metric contradicts Table 3’s readability scores.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents fuzzy keyword versus exact metadata matching, distributed vLLM processing on eight A100 80GB GPUs, processing costs, and concurrent query execution. It also supplies dedicated Hugging Face and ModelScope dataset links, although Appendix D still describes release prospectively. The detailed prompts and clustering hyperparameters already appeared in v1.

R1.justification: The same 43 cited works and largely unchanged related-work discussion are retained. v2 adds explicit positioning against SurveyX, contrasting its general survey automation with ResearchDB’s retrieval of technical specifics.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, author/front-matter text, expands Section 3.2, rewrites the evaluation discussion and conclusion, and adds an ablation subsection. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact. Corpus and schema documentation is moved from the appendix into the main text.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a predominantly single-column design with a boxed title block and colored headings. v1 Tables A3 and A2 become v2 Tables 1 and 2; existing plots are grouped into multipanel figures and the appendix tree is enlarged. v2 also adds a retrieval diagram and ablation table and redraws the comparison radar chart to include SurveyX.

improvement.justification: The SurveyX comparison, component ablations, and efficiency disclosures provide useful empirical support and practical information missing from v1. The gain is limited by reporting problems: Section 5.1 claims superiority on every metric although Table 3 shows lower readability, and attributes the largest accuracy drop to removing dynamic weighting although abstract-only retrieval drops further. Unexplained radar-score revisions and removal of the earlier tradeoff discussion also weaken interpretive clarity.
